market_specific_notes: Boston has an unusually high concentration of teaching hospitals, and a hospital's reputation says nothing about whether a particular physician inside it holds a USCIS civil surgeon designation. Designation is held by named doctors, and the federal locator is where that is recorded.

USCIS recognises all state and local health departments as civil surgeons for one specific purpose — completing “the vaccination assessments for refugees seeking adjustment of status”. In Boston that body is the Boston Public Health Commission. It covers vaccinations for that category, not the full examination for everyone.

USCIS also warns that “Many health insurance plans do not cover all portions of this examination.” Bring the card, then ask whether the practice accepts the plan for immigration medical examinations specifically.

Do not confuse the two places. The immigration medical examination is done by a civil surgeon in a private practice. The USCIS field office is where, in its own words, it holds “Interviews for all non-asylum cases (for example, getting a Green Card)” and “Naturalization ceremonies”. Boston's is in the John F. Kennedy Federal Building at 15 New Sudbury Street. The civil surgeon is somewhere else, and the two appointments are unrelated.
Start the checklist below with the federal locator rather than a hospital name. Designation belongs to named doctors, and the locator is the only record of it.
local_vetting_points: Search uscis.gov/tools/find-a-civil-surgeon by ZIP code, and treat the result as the designation record rather than a recommendation.
Confirm the practice appears in the federal locator under the name it bills and answers the phone under.
Ask whether tuberculosis testing is done on site and what a positive result does to the price and the timeline.
Ask what the office does when a vaccination record cannot be produced.
Ask who signs the completed form and how long after the visit.
typical_cost_ranges: No authority publishes a price. USCIS: “Fees for immigration medical examinations are established by the civil surgeon. Fees may vary by civil surgeon.”

A hospital-based practice and a standalone clinic can bill this differently. Ask whether anything will arrive as a separate facility or laboratory charge after the visit, and get the answer before you book.
Ask for five figures separately: examination, tuberculosis and syphilis testing, missing vaccines, completing and sealing the form, and any follow-up.
Form I-693 has no USCIS filing fee — $0. The published sum is the underlying I-485: paper $1,440 or online $1,390 for an applicant over 14.
payment_options: USCIS instructs applicants to check acceptable forms of payment beforehand. In a hospital setting also ask whether any part is billed afterwards rather than collected on the day.
Ask whether a laboratory charge could arrive separately from the practice's own bill.
wait_time_notes: In a hospital system the examination and the paperwork can sit with different teams. Ask who releases the completed form and how you collect it.
Ask what the usual gap is between the visit and a signed form when records are complete.
availability_notes: Confirm whether a same-week appointment refers to the examination or to the completed paperwork.
If a filing deadline is close, name the date on the call and ask the office to commit or decline.
named_resources_or_providers: USCIS Find a Civil Surgeon locator (official) — uscis.gov/tools/find-a-civil-surgeon
the Boston Public Health Commission — boston.gov/departments/boston-public-health-commission. USCIS recognises local health departments as civil surgeons for the refugee vaccination assessment.

USCIS Boston field office (BOS) — John F. Kennedy Federal Building, 15 New Sudbury St., Room E-160, Boston, MA 02203. From the USCIS field office ZIP data file at uscis.gov/about-us/find-a-uscis-office/field-offices.

Massachusetts Immunization Information System (MIIS), via myvaxrecords.mass.gov — the state describes it as where you “Request, view and print your vaccination records” from the official MIIS. The page publishes no eligibility rule.
Massachusetts Department of Public Health, Tuberculosis — mass.gov/tuberculosis.
USCIS Form I-693 page — uscis.gov/i-693, for the current form edition and filing instructions.
Listings are neutral examples and starting points for your own verification. Nothing here is a ranking or an endorsement.
city_intro_override: In Boston the instinct is to work outward from a well-known hospital. The civil surgeon designation does not work that way: it belongs to individual designated doctors, and the only authoritative list is the federal locator. Start there and let reputation be the second question.

primary_city_decision_block.title: Local civil surgeon comparison checklist
items: Verify designation in the official USCIS locator before comparing anything else.
Ask for the price broken into examination, labs, vaccines, form completion and follow-up.
Gather the vaccination records USCIS names before the first visit.
Ask what a positive tuberculosis test would do to the cost and the schedule.
Tell the office whether the I-485 is going by mail or online.
Confirm the form edition and the date the civil surgeon intends to sign.

heading: Boston: designation belongs to doctors, not to hospitals
i693_document_requirements: Form I-693 in the edition USCIS currently accepts.

Government-issued photo identification such as a valid passport or driver's licence. For an applicant aged 14 or younger, USCIS accepts identification showing name, date and place of birth and a parent's full name — a birth certificate with an English translation, or an affidavit.

A record of your vaccinations or immunisations, covering what USCIS names: DT, DTP, DTaP, Td, Tdap, OPV, IPV, MMR, Hib, Hepatitis A, Hepatitis B, Varicella, Pneumococcal, Influenza, Rotavirus and Meningococcal disease.
Your health insurance card, with the coverage question already prepared.
Payment, in a form the office has told you it accepts.
vaccination_handling_notes: The records are the cheapest part of this process to get right and the most expensive to get wrong.
Massachusetts runs the MIIS, and myvaxrecords.mass.gov is the state route to your own record. It does not state who may request one, so allow time in case you have to go back to individual practices.
Records collected before you book are worth more than any price difference between two offices.
Massachusetts operates a statewide immunisation information system through which residents can request their own record; ask the clinic what record format it accepts before you order.
Refugees adjusting status may complete the vaccination assessment at a state or local health department under the USCIS blanket designation described above.
bilingual_support: The USCIS locator filters by Languages Spoken from a long list of named languages, and by doctor's sex. Both entries come from the practice's declaration to USCIS.
A language listed in the tool tells you it exists in the practice. Ask separately whether it covers the paperwork review, which is where a misunderstanding becomes a correction.
appointment_booking_notes: Decide before the exam how the I-485 is being filed. By mail the envelope stays sealed. Online, USCIS instructs you to open it and upload the form, then keep the original and the envelope until the case is decided.
Confirm the form edition and the intended signing date. Only the 01/20/25 edition is accepted for signatures dated 3 July 2025 or later.
Ask whether the slot you are offered is intake, examination, or the full path to a signed form.
Ask who releases the sealed packet and how a correction is handled once it has left the practice. In a hospital system the answer often involves a different department from the one that examined you.
